The application to Judah by name, “Behold, I frame evil against you” (web:Jer.18.11), turns the same consonantal root into a verb rather than repeating the noun: הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤ר עֲלֵיכֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) is a bare participle, byte-distinct from the article-bearing noun that names the craftsman at 18:2, 18:3, 18:4 and 18:6 (sweep: 5 verses on the article-bearing form); the shared object is the article-free spelling itself, and that spelling recurs across the book (sweep: 10 verses on that spelling). boundary_rationale: A fresh command opens the row: “Go, and buy a potter’s earthen container, and take some of the elders of the people and of the elders of the priests” (web:Jer.19.1), spliced הָל֛וֹךְ וְקָנִ֥יתָ בַקְבֻּ֖ק יוֹצֵ֣ר חָ֑רֶשׂ וּמִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וּמִזִּקְנֵ֖י הַכֹּהֲנִֽים (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier), the command opening after the messenger formula on an infinitive absolute and a waw-prefixed second-person-singular suffix-conjugation form, not an imperative, opening on the prophet as addressee and distinct from the potter-house visit that precedes it and from the prophet’s own petition just before it, building a new commissioned sign on a jar rather than clay on a wheel. The command names the errand (buy the jar, go out to the valley of Ben-Hinnom, 19:1-2) and the oracle to proclaim there (19:3-9), then turns to the performance instruction, “Then you shall break the container in the sight of the men who go with you” (web:Jer.19.10), before its own interpretation, כָּ֣כָה אֶשְׁבֹּ֞ר אֶת הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְאֶת הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁבֹּר֙ אֶת כְּלִ֣י הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.19.11, byte tier) — “Even so I will break this people and this city as one breaks a potter’s vessel” (web:Jer.19.11) — closing on the Topheth-house judgment through 19:13. Command, performance instruction, and interpretation stay one unit because the same errand and the same named jar carry through from the buying to the breaking to the verdict on the houses of Jerusalem; the elders of the people and of the priests, וּמִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וּמִזִּקְנֵ֖י הַכֹּהֲנִֽים (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier), are named as taken along on the errand in the rendering, with no verb in the Hebrew governing that clause, and the witnesses at the breaking are instead הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַהֹלְכִ֖ים אוֹתָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.19.10, byte tier), the men who go with the prophet.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through Jeremiah’s public proclamation in the temple court (19:14-15) was considered: that scene still reports the same errand’s outcome, but it relocates from the valley of Ben-Hinnom to the court of Yahweh’s house and turns from the elders taken along to “all the people” (web:Jer.19.14), a scene-and-addressee shift treated here as the stronger seam.
literature_type_guess: enacted sign-act narrative: a shattered potter’s jar in the Hinnom valley pronouncing an unmendable verdict on Jerusalem

boundary_rationale: A sworn divine oath opens the row, חַי אָנִי֮ נְאֻם יְהוָה֒ כִּ֣י אִם יִהְיֶ֞ה כָּנְיָ֤הוּ בֶן יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה חוֹתָ֖ם עַל יַ֣ד יְמִינִ֑י כִּ֥י מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶתְּקֶֽנְךָּ (oshb:Jer.22.24, byte tier) — “As I live,” says Yahweh, “though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet on my right hand, I would still pluck you from there” (web:Jer.22.24) — a chai-ani oath formula distinct from the imperative apostrophe just closed, and naming the king in the form כָּנְיָ֤הוּ, also attested at Jer.22.28 and Jer.37.1, apart from the Jehoiachin form at Jer.52.31 and the Jeconiah form at Jer.24.1, Jer.27.20, Jer.28.4 and Jer.29.2. As elsewhere in this book, WLC stands behind these marks unaccompanied, so what the Prophets afford here is tier-3, weak corroboration. One paseq seg stands at Jer.23.6 (count-only, single-witness, no intra-verse position claim). The announcement formula הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה opens Jer.23.5 (oshb:Jer.23.5, byte tier) and its lachen-prefixed shape לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה opens Jer.23.7 (oshb:Jer.23.7, byte tier), both immediately after the setumahs named above; the formula is book-wide (sweep: 15 verses, MT keys), not local color. The closing pair Jer.23.7-Jer.23.8 shares an identical seven-word consonantal opening with Jer.16.14-Jer.16.15 and, after one divergent verb, an identical sixteen-word consonantal run (skeleton tier) -- cross-seam texture, disclosed here and not treated as a boundary driver. This material opens on the woe formula against the shepherds and reads closest to a woe oracle for that opening, though its own bulk turns from indictment to a salvation promise once the shepherds are sentenced in Jer.23.1-Jer.23.2.

boundary_rationale: A fresh topic opens the row: “Concerning the prophets: My heart within me is broken.” (web:Jer.23.9), splicing לַנְּבִאִ֞ים נִשְׁבַּ֧ר לִבִּ֣י בְקִרְבִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.23.9, byte tier) -- turning from the shepherd-and-Branch promise to a new subject, the prophets, with the prophet's own first-person distress replacing the direct divine voice of the material just before it. The charge against prophet and priest together (Jer.23.11) narrows into the named comparison between Samaria's prophets and Jerusalem's prophets (Jer.23.13-Jer.23.14) and closes on the formal sentence against them at Jer.23.15; no addressee shift or fresh imperative interrupts this sequence from the opening distress to the closing sentence, so the whole span stays one unit. The row's own close at Jer.23.15 carries no neum-YHWH token (byte tier, oshb:Jer.23.15); its two in-span occurrences (sweep: 2 verses in this span: Jer.23.11, Jer.23.12) both stand verse-finally inside the span, closing only their own verses rather than this unit, and what closes the unit instead is the sentence introduced by the messenger formula, “Therefore Yahweh of Armies says concerning the prophets:” (web:Jer.23.15), splicing לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ עַל הַנְּבִאִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.23.15, byte tier).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving Jer.23.13-Jer.23.14's Samaria/Jerusalem comparison its own row was considered, since it names a specific pair of cities; but the indicting first person there is the divine speaker's, continuing without a break the ki-subordinated clause opened at Jer.23.11 (the prophet's own distress at Jer.23.9 names Yahweh only in the third person), and it feeds directly into the sentence pronounced at Jer.23.15.
literature_type_guess: prophetic-anguish indictment of Samaria's and Jerusalem's prophets, closing in a formal sentence
